author: reek
body: A lease is a loan, and this is the test that it is asked for again. The acquisition test proves an address arrives; nothing in it would notice a client that took one and held it forever, which is what this tree did until 2026-07-30.

author: reek
body: IT NEEDS A SHORT LEASE TO BE A TEST AT ALL. Renewal happens at half the lease, so against the default hour nothing observable happens inside a run: the sidecar asks codex-vm for a four-second lease, T1 is two seconds, and the spin below covers it several times over.

author: reek
body: THE ROWS ARE CHOSEN SO A CLIENT THAT DOES NOTHING FAILS THEM. `due before` must be no, because a lease taken a moment ago is not due, and a test whose first row was already yes would pass on a broken clock. `due after wait` must be yes, or the spin did not outlast T1 and the renewal that follows proves nothing. `renewed` compares lease-start, which only an accepted ACK moves.

author: reek
body: The wait is a spin on the clock rather than a count of turns, because what has to elapse is SECONDS and the turns-per-second of this loop is whatever the machine happens to give. Each turn reads the HPET, which is a VM exit, so the host advances its models and can answer.
